body: A book of 100 pages, printed in full colour with pictures and diagrams, written by Reiss Davies Ausar. It is one of two books by him on this shelf.
The listing describes it as written for all reading levels. That is a statement about the reading, not about the reader.
A page count, a colour, an author and a price. Those four rows are the whole of the physical description.
No binding, no ISBN, no publisher, no year, no page size and no language. Those rows say not printed on the sheet below, and they stay that way until somebody prints them.

acc.summary: What this page does not say
body: The listing sets out at length what the book is meant to do for whoever reads it. None of that is repeated here, in those words or in any others.
The subject is the one the title names. What the book argues about it is in the book, which is where an argument belongs.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The specification of a book is a page count, a binding, a colour, an author and a price. This one has four of the five. What the pages argue is not a specification, it is the book, and a shop page that summarised it would be making the argument on the book's behalf without any of the room the book has to make it properly.

reiss.label: From Reiss
reiss.h2: Why the page will not summarise it
paras: I wrote it, which is the one line on this page I can give you without going back to a listing to check. What it sets out to do is in the 100 pages. If I put that here instead, in two sentences on a page with a buy button under them, the sentences would be doing a job they are not allowed to do on a shop page in Britain.

So the sheet gives you a page count, a colour, an author and a price, and tells you plainly that the binding and the ISBN are missing. If you want to know whether the book is for you, ring the shop and ask me, or read the journal, which is the same voice for nothing.
reiss.pull: If you want to know whether the book is for you, ring the shop and ask me.
